#### 1. hereditary chronic pancreatitis  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.500)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9925561)

**Proposed mechanism:** SPINK1 (HGNC:11244) —DECREASES→ pancreatic enzyme activation (REACT:R-HSA-193837); PRSS1 (HGNC:9810) —DISRUPTS→ pancreatic enzyme activation (REACT:R-HSA-193837); pancreatic enzyme activation (REACT:R-HSA-193837) —LEADS_TO→ pancreatitis (HP:0002217); pancreatic enzyme activation (REACT:R-HSA-193837) —LEADS_TO→ chronic pancreatitis (HP:0001100). Loss-of-function mutations in SPINK1 reduce its ability to inhibit premature pancreatic enzyme activation, contributing to tropical pancreatitis. Gain-of-function mutations in PRSS1 lead to auto-activation of trypsinogen, causing premature pancreatic enzyme activation and hereditary chronic pancreatitis. Both pathways converge on the dysregulation of pancreatic enzyme activation, ultimately leading to pancreatitis.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of mutations in SPINK1 and PRSS1 in patients diagnosed with tropical pancreatitis or hereditary chronic pancreatitis, respectively, would falsify this hypothesis. Furthermore, if genetic analysis reveals that the mutations in SPINK1 are gain-of-function and PRSS1 are loss-of-function, this would contradict the proposed mechanism. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD showing high allele frequency (>1%) for pathogenic variants in SPINK1 and PRSS1 in general populations would challenge their role as rare disease-causing genes.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathway of pancreatic enzyme dysregulation highlights potential therapeutic strategies targeting protease inhibition or activation pathways that could be beneficial for both forms of pancreatitis.
